newsitem.title: USA: Egyptian envoy has sideline role in Mideast talks.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian envoy has sideline role in Mideast talks.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa will come to Washington for a summit designed to end Israeli-Palestinian clashes but will not take a direct part in the talks, the State Department said on Monday.

"He will be in Washington available for consultations with the parties ... Foreign Minister Moussa will not be a direct participant in the talks. That is the choice of the Egyptian government," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

The White House said Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak would not attend the summit hosted by U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday and Wednesday. Mubarak had been invited along with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and King Hussein of Jordan.

Secretary of State Warren Christopher said it "would have been good if President Mubarak had been able to come" but Washington appreciated Moussa's coming. Egypt would continue to play a major role in the Middle East peace process, he said.
Christopher said it was clear that "the Middle East peace process is in a state of crisis". He said "the parties are quite estranged and raw because of the violence and killings."

He said the objectives of the summit were that the Israelis and Palestinians would begin to talk together again, that they would commit to end the violence and that they would find a basis for resuming peace negotiations.
